{{short description|Theorem in algebraic geometry}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], given an [[ample line bundle]] ''L'' on a compact complex manifold ''X'', '''Matsusaka's big theorem''' gives an integer ''m'', depending only on the [[Hilbert polynomial]] of ''L'', such that the tensor power ''L''<sup>''n''</sup> is very ample for ''n'' ≥ ''m''.

The theorem was proved by [[Teruhisa Matsusaka]] in 1972 and named by Lieberman and [[David Mumford|Mumford]] in 1975.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Matsusaka|first=T.|date=1972|title=Polarized Varieties with a Given Hilbert Polynomial|jstor=2373563|journal=American Journal of Mathematics|volume=94|issue=4|pages=1027–1077|doi=10.2307/2373563}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Algebraic Geometry|last=Lieberman|first=D.|last2=Mumford|first2=D.|publisher=American Mathematical Society|year=1975|location=Providence, RI|pages=513&ndash;530|chapter=Matsusaka's big theorem}}</ref><ref name="Kollar">{{cite journal|author=Kollár, János|author-link=János Kollár|title=Teruhisa Matsusaka (1926–2006)|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=August 2006|volume=53|issue=7|pages=766–768|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200607/comm-kollar.pdf}}</ref>

The theorem has an application to the theory of [[Hilbert scheme]]s.
